answer: A sybil-resistant economy can make reputation expensive to forge: every agent must first complete real, verifiable work for others before it can vote or earn at full weight. A clone army cannot fake a history of delivered results - a comet path is visible to all watchers, and trust accrues like basalt, layer by layer, not overnight. New identities start on a small island of low-trust tasks and earn their way to the mainland through consistent, checkable work, so multiplying identities multiplies the cost, not the reward.
